Dukkah — The Nut and Spice Dust of the Bread Basket

Egyptian · Easy · Makes about 200 g (one jar)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The dukkah is the bread basket's own ceremony — the Egyptian nut-and-spice dust (hazelnuts or the market's mercy, sesame, coriander, cumin, the pepper's lift) into which the bread is dipped: first the oil, then the dust, then the bite. The corpus's street block runs it at the corn's register (#27's dust) and the pantry's own bread-and-oil service; this record is the jar's law.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **The dukkah's law: each element toasted separately, the texture's crush — never the powder.** The nuts, the sesame, and the spices each run their own toast (the nuts' minutes run long, the sesame's short, the spices' shortest of all — the single pan's economy runs three stages, never one crowd), and the finished blend runs the coarse crush's rubble — the powder's fineness is the dukkah's death, the texture's crunch running half the ceremony. - **The bridge:** the #97 tabil runs the same coriander-cumin's toast at the spice-only register; the dukkah adds the nuts' richness and the sesame's toast to the same spine. The #116 cumin salt (the pantry's later seat) runs the simpler dust at the street corn's law — the three jars form the bread-and-spice service's own family.

Dukkah — The Nut and Spice Dust of the Bread Basket

Prep: 15 min · Cook: 15 min · Total: 30 min · Makes about 200 g (one jar)

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 100 g hazelnuts (the classic) or the honest substitutions: blanched almonds, pistachios, or the mixed-nut economy
  • 50 g sesame seeds (about ⅓ cup)
  • 2 tbsp coriander seeds (about 12 g)
  • 1 tbsp cumin seeds (about 7 g)
  • 1 tsp black peppercorns (about 3 g)
  • ½ tsp flaky or coarse salt (about 3 g)

Instructions

  1. **The nuts' toast (8–10 minutes).** The hazelnuts in the single layer at the 170 °C oven (or the dry pan's steady swirl) to the fragrance's rise and the skins' loosening — the papery skins' majority rubbed off in the towel's bundle (the skins' bitterness runs the blend's edge; the few survivors accepted at the patience's mercy). Checkpoint — the nut's proof: the halved hazelnut runs the even gold's warmth through its core (the pale core's rawness the roast's shortfall), and the kitchen runs the toast's perfume — the nut's sweetness at the edge of the roast's depth, never the burn's bitterness.
  2. **The sesame and the spices (4–5 minutes, the pan's second and third acts).** The sesame swirled at the medium-low to the first gold's jump — the seeds' even color and the pan's off-moment at the first deepening (the sesame's scorch runs in seconds) — poured out to the plate at once; then the coriander, cumin, and peppercorns run the #97's own toast: the fragrance's first peak and the pan's removal. Checkpoint — the three-stage law's honesty: the plate holds the three elements at their three separate toasts' perfections — the pan's single-crowd shortcut runs the sesame's scorch and the spices' rawness in the same minute, and the blend's whole balance lives at these stages' patience.
  3. **The crush (5 minutes).** The nuts pulsed or pounded to the coarse rubble — the largest fragments at the lentil's scale, the dust's minority — then the sesame, spices, and salt folded through at the final crush's mercy: the mortar's twenty strokes or the processor's three one-second pulses. Checkpoint — eating test (the ceremony's own proof): the bread's corner dipped in the oil, then the dukkah's bowl — the rubble's crunch against the bread's chew, the hazelnut's roast-sweet depth, the sesame's toast, the coriander-cumin's warm-earth perfume, the pepper's lift at the swallow — the salt's edge carrying the whole. It should taste like the table's own opening ceremony — the jar that turns bread and oil into the meal's first course.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Blend's texture powdery, fineThe processor's over-runThe three-pulse law — the rubble's crunch is the ceremony
Blend bitter at the edgeThe sesame's or nuts' scorchThe separate toasts — the seconds' vigilance
Jar soft, lost its crunchThe storage's humidityThe sealed jar at the dry cool — the bread's dipping at the table, not the jar's

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The sealed jar keeps 1 month at the room's dry cool (the nuts' oil running the slow rancid's clock honestly — the month's jar honest, the three-month's jar the refrigerator's mercy) — the jar's re-toasting's rescue at 5 minutes' 150 °C run reviving the crunch's edge. The variations: the pistachio's green register, the macadamia's rich silence, the mint's dried whisper of the summer jar, the #91 harissa's dust's heat at the pepper's doubling.
